title: Stadium Juggle Challenge
premise: A fast arcade soccer-juggling game where the player keeps a glowing football airborne inside a floodlit night stadium for as long as possible.
interaction_model: Single-screen pointer/touch arcade play; tap or click directly on the ball to kick it upward and steer its drift.
objective: Achieve the highest possible consecutive juggle count before the ball hits the ground.
progression: Run-based score chasing with escalating difficulty emerging from ball momentum, drift correction, and streak pressure rather than discrete levels.
likely_audience: Casual players, mobile arcade fans, and players who enjoy short reflex-based skill games.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is a single-screen soccer juggling score attack because the title, HUD labels, and scoring logic all align.
High confidence in the tap/click control model because the ball reacts directly to pointer position with upward force, lateral correction, and spin.
Moderate confidence in the broader 'neon derby' flavor because it appears mainly in presentation text and visual styling rather than unique rule systems.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen arcade soccer juggling game called 'Stadium Juggle Challenge' set in a dramatic night stadium under floodlights. The player should use mouse clicks or touchscreen taps directly on a soccer ball to keep it airborne for as long as possible, with every successful touch counting as one juggle. The ball must obey simple but readable physics: gravity pulls it down constantly, taps give it a strong upward kick, and off-center hits add sideways velocity and spin so the player has to correct drift over time. The round begins from a stylish start screen, switches into an active HUD showing the current juggle count, and ends instantly when the ball touches the ground, followed by a game-over panel with the final score and a quick retry button. Present the action on a full-screen canvas with a glowing sports-broadcast look: dark blue night sky, misty clouds, a lit stadium horizon, green turf, a ball shadow, particle bursts on successful hits, and subtle combo celebration effects. Add satisfying audio with looping background music, kick sounds on each hit, a bonus combo cue every few juggles, and a fail sound on game over. Include small streak messages and celebratory reaction visuals to reward longer runs, but keep the overall structure minimal, replayable, responsive on mobile, and focused on pure reflex-based score chasing.
